evidence: Cic. Caecin. 13: aliquem introitū prohibēre (Lewis & Short)
Tac. H. 1.31: prīmō statim introitū (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The noun of introīre; also the entrance itself (see entry, the way in). Latin as often says it with a verb: ingressus, cum intrāret, “on his entry” (see enter).

terms.gloss: an entering; also a walking, a gait
terms.comment: “Entering” from the early Empire on (Vell., Plin.; Lewis & Short); Cicero uses it of walking and the way one walks (tarditātibus in ingressū mollioribus, Off. 1.131). Quintilian has in ingressū for the beginning of a speech or a book.

phrases.latin: nocturnus introitus Zmyrnam quasi in hostium urbem
phrases.english: a night-time entry into Smyrna, as if into an enemy city

phrases.latin: haec in ipsō ingressū meō scrīpsī
phrases.english: I wrote this the moment I arrived (in the province)
